reason: The lens needs a holder so it can slide into focus.
expectation: The lens and holder will form an adjustable projection lens assembly.

effect: The lens is now in an adjustable assembly, ready to fit to the theatre.
reason: The theatre needs the lens assembly to project and focus its stars.
expectation: The lens assembly will attach to the theatre so its projection can be focused.

effect: The lens is installed, and its slider can be used to compare focus settings once the cloth is hung.
reaction: The intended focus test is clearer now.
reason: The projector needs the hanging cloth as a screen.
expectation: The cloth will provide a surface for the projected stars.

effect: The cloth is in place, and sliding the lens brings the star-disc image into focus.
reaction: Comparing blurry and sharp settings makes the lens’s role clear.
reason: The dark hood should fit around the projection lens and limit stray light.
expectation: The hood will shade the lens and help keep unwanted light off the projection.

alternatives.reason: The handle should turn the star wheel, but I would fit the hood first.

effect: The hood reduces stray light and makes the projected stars stand out against darker spaces.
reaction: The improvement in contrast makes the hood’s purpose clear.
reason: The star wheel needs its handle to turn the projected sky.
expectation: The handle will turn the star wheel and move the projected stars.

effect: The handle completed the star theatre: turning it moves the projected stars, and the finished image is upside down.
reaction: The inverted image was a small, interesting surprise.

mostWorthwhile.text: Setting up the cloth and sliding the lens was most worthwhile: comparing blurry and sharp images made the projector's focusing mechanism concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the lens to its holder was straightforward preparation, but less revealing than seeing it focus the image.

surprise.text: The completed projection was upside down, even though that did not matter for the invented constellations.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; each piece had a clear role in constructing or operating the projector.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the focus and contrast tests made the construction feel useful to understand, and I am curious how the fair will bring the inventions together.
